### 📓 Docs Drift Check
Nothing in this diff resolved to a documentable surface (no symbol, route or SDK anchor derived from **1** changed package(s)), so **this run has no opinion** about the docs.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `os serve (command, 38 pages)`
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **30** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 23540582f4f7a783ee11337bbda12a8352a70f91` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `6531b3324328c3310f23e01f66abe5933129758d`
Local-runs: none
Scope: .changeset/25133-refuse-orgless-production-boot.md, content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx, content/docs/upgrading.mdx, packages/cli/src/commands/serve.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/serve-kernel-only-lifetime.integration.test.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/serve-no-server-banner.integration.test.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/serve-no-transport-announcements.integration.test.ts, packages/cli/test/serve-no-auth-secret-refusal.integration.test.ts, packages/cli/test/serve-no-storage-boot-guard.integration.test.ts, packages/cli/test/serve-ready-degraded-boot.e2e.test.ts; read to judge them: packages/core/src/stack-auth.ts, packages/core/src/kernel.ts, packages/runtime/src/runtime.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/start.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/dev.ts, packages/cli/test/helpers/serve-process.ts, packages/cli/test/serve-migrate-exit-schema-parity.integration.test.ts, .changeset/24583-7b3-organizationless-counter-retired.md, content/docs/releases/v18/index.mdx, content/docs/automation/webhooks.mdx, packages/cli/CHANGELOG.md, scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs, scripts/measure-test-shard-timings.mjs, AGENTS.md

Read-only. The head `6531b332` was checked out in a detached worktree from `origin/claude/issue-25133-refuse-orgless-production-boot` (merge-base with `origin/main` `23540582f4` is `4c7dcb4519`) and diffed against that merge-base: 10 files, +346 / -81. The ruling 6328987873 (seven binding items), the seat's effort note 6328820987, the claim 6329345390, both dev reports (6330211620, superseded by 6330837413), the measurement 6323585273 section 2 and the PR body were read from the GitHub API; the check-runs for the head were read the same way; `node scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs --branch ...` was run (read-only). Nothing was built, no test was run, nothing was posted. The ablation counts are judged structurally from the pins, not re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

**Item 1 (ruling item 1, letter A).** Executed as ruled, for both compositions, with or without `--server`.
- No-auth case (`auth` tier off, no AuthPlugin mounted): `packages/cli/src/commands/serve.ts:4674-4675` sets `const productionBoot = !isDev;` and the condition is `(flags.server || productionBoot) && !(tierEnabled('auth') || hasAuthPlugin)` — a production boot is refused regardless of the flag; a development boot keeps the old `flags.server` gate, as the ruling leaves `--dev` unchanged. `isDev` is `isDevelopmentBoot(flags.dev)` (`serve.ts:2414`; `packages/core/src/stack-auth.ts:135-137`: `--dev` or `NODE_ENV === 'development'`).
- No-secret case: `serve.ts:4704` is now `!authComposition.composes && authComposition.reason === 'no-secret'` with the `flags.server` guard removed. The dev's claim that `no-secret` is production-only holds by construction: `resolveAuthSecret({ isDev })` returns the fallback on every development boot (`stack-auth.ts:145-148`), and `resolvePlatformAuthComposition` returns `no-secret` only when `secret` is undefined (`stack-auth.ts:184`).
- Before any plugin starts: both throws precede `await runtime.start()` (`serve.ts:5423`); `runtime.use` → `ObjectKernel.use` only registers (`packages/core/src/kernel.ts:347-377`, state must be `idle`, no init or start), and the `OS_MIGRATE_AND_EXIT=1` short-circuit sits after `runtime.start()` (`serve.ts:5491`), so a migrate-and-exit job meets the same throw before the kernel bootstraps. The pins prove the SQLite file is never created on a refused leg (`packages/cli/test/serve-no-auth-secret-refusal.integration.test.ts:159`) and is created on every control leg (`:169`), including the `OS_MIGRATE_AND_EXIT=1` leg (`:209-219`).
- Both texts drop the "run with --no-server" remedy (`serve.ts:4680-4683`, `:4709-4712`) and each now says kernel-only does not avoid the refusal; the pin asserts the old phrase "serve without the data API" is absent (`:158`).
- `host-kernel` stays warn-only: the reason is resolved before `no-secret` (`stack-auth.ts:181-184`), so the no-secret refusal cannot fire there; the warn is unchanged at `serve.ts:4160-4164`, and the control leg asserts it (`:238-245`). Note the `host-kernel` reason requires the `auth` tier on; a host kernel with the tier off is `auth-tier-off` and is refused under the no-auth condition (see B3).
- `os dev` hands `--dev` to `serve` (`packages/cli/src/commands/dev.ts:781-782`); programmatic embedding never runs this command. Unchanged.
- `os start`: spawns `serve` with no `--server`/`--no-server` flag at all (`packages/cli/src/commands/start.ts:524-534`) and always with a secret (`start.ts:315-317`, `AUTH_SECRET` at `:455`), so it reaches only the no-auth refusal, which already fired under `--server` on main. Unchanged by this PR.
- Other production shapes: `--preset minimal` resolves tiers `['core']` (`stack-auth.ts:62`) → `auth-tier-off` → refused either way. A config that mounts its own HonoServer with `--no-server`: the refusal reads no transport, so it is refused iff no auth composes. `--no-server` with `NODE_ENV=development` is a development boot and is not refused. A stack that mounts its own AuthPlugin is `stack-supplies-auth` and composes an organization object; outside the ruling's two cases.
- Still not refused, outside the ruling's two named compositions: the `auth` tier on with a secret set, but `@objectstack/plugin-auth` fails to load — `serve.ts:4573-4579` warns and boots on with no AuthPlugin and no organization object (B2). An install failure, not a configuration; pre-existing on main.
- Nothing legitimate refused: a production boot with a secret reaches ready with and without `--server` (pins `:221`, `:225`), `--dev` boots (`:234`, `:265`), the host kernel boots (`:238`).

**Item 2 (ruling item 2).** No "tenant-scoped objects present" qualifier: neither condition reads the object set or any `tenancy` declaration (`serve.ts:4675`, `:4704`). The changeset states that `tenancy: { enabled: false }` does not lift the refusal, which is true of the code.

**Item 3 (the consequence the dev flags).** A production `os serve --preset minimal` is refused with or without `--server` unless the stack mounts AuthPlugin: this follows item 1 as written, since `minimal` is `['core']` and the no-auth condition is exactly "tier off, no AuthPlugin". Documentation: the changeset FROM/TO covers it only generically ("when the stack mounted no auth at all") and never names `--preset minimal`; in `cli.mdx` every `--preset minimal` mention is unchanged — `:358` ("Skip auto-loaded auth/i18n/ui plugins"), `:375`, and the tier table `:395` (`minimal | core | none`) — and the sentence at `:399-401` still says "The `auth` tier requires `OS_AUTH_SECRET` to be set; otherwise `AuthPlugin` is skipped with a yellow warning", which contradicts the paragraph the PR wrote at `:365-371`. `git grep -n "preset minimal" origin/main -- content/docs packages/cli/src` lists `cli.mdx:358`, `:369`, `webhooks.mdx:130` (messaging only, still true), `serve.ts:632`, `:1476`, `:2925`, `security-catalog-overlays.ts:130` and `schema-migration-plugins.ts:1934`; none is annotated on the branch (B1).

**Item 4 (ruling item 3, pins).** All present in `serve-no-auth-secret-refusal.integration.test.ts`: no-secret with `--server` (`:198`), no-secret `--no-server` (`:202`), no-secret `--no-server` + `OS_MIGRATE_AND_EXIT=1` (`:209`), no-auth with `--server` (`:249`), no-auth `--no-server` with a secret (`:253`); controls: a configured secret with and without `--server` (`:221`, `:225`), `--dev --no-server` (`:234`), `host-kernel --no-server` asserting the warn line (`:238`), no-auth `--dev --no-server` (`:265`). Every leg spawns `bin/run.js` with `NODE_ENV: undefined` written after the leg's env (`:118-122`); `childEnv` spreads overrides last and `spawn` omits undefined entries (`packages/cli/test/helpers/serve-process.ts:881-889`), so production posture cannot be overridden. Refused legs prove nothing was written by the absent database file (`:159`) against controls that create it (`:169`). Ablation, judged structurally: putting `flags.server &&` back on the no-secret condition leaves `:198` green and reds `:202` and `:209` — 2 red; on the no-auth condition it reds `:253` only — 1 red. Matches the dev's stated 2 / 1. Nothing was removed from the pre-PR file: its two legs survive with every assertion (`git diff` against the merge-base), plus the new absent-remedy assertion. The four re-fixtured files each still test their own purpose: `serve-no-server-banner` (`:302-311`, `:349-354`) and `serve-no-transport-announcements` (`:302-315`, `:364-369`) boot today's production kernel-only command (default tiers, a secret, a store) and keep `expectNoServerShape`, `expectDatasourceAdminDegradeLine`, the no-`objectstack:listening` and no-state-file assertions, and the config-mounted-HonoServer control; `serve-kernel-only-lifetime` shape 1 (`:282-288`) keeps the defect's mechanism (no storage driver, so no pool) on a host-kernel stub with `tiers: ['core', 'auth']` and still `--preset minimal`, with the held-then-SIGTERM-exit-0 assertion intact; `serve-no-storage-boot-guard` case 2 (`:274-277`) keeps "one line before any start() and the banner still reached" on the same stub. `serve-ready-degraded-boot.e2e` moves its degraded leg onto the host-kernel stub and keeps the healthy leg on the bare config with a secret; the discriminating assertion ("an always-append implementation passes the degraded leg and fails here") still holds, and the header says the legs now differ in config as well as secret. No test weakened.

**Item 5 (ruling item 5, counting).** Census at the head: 16 cli test files name `--no-server`; 7 are unit-level with no spawn (`serve-datasource-admin-routes`, `serve-http-server-composition`, `serve-kernel-only-hold`, `serve-no-transport-announcements.test`, `serve-observability-registration`, `serve-unknown-hostname-guard`, `format.server-ready-no-http-server`); the two under `migrate/` carry `--dev` and a secret; `serve-migrate-exit-schema-parity.integration` spawns `CLI` from `helpers/serve-process.js`, which is `bin/run-dev.js` (`serve-process.ts:21-22`, pins `NODE_ENV=development`), so it is a development boot and is rightly untouched. The dev counted first (PR body, report 6330211620); the flag-times-secret method missed the four `--preset minimal` files because each carries `--dev` or `OS_AUTH_SECRET` in other legs; CI on `5996c531` caught them and `6531b332` re-fixtured exactly those four plus the nightly e2e. Only real production boots were re-fixtured. The PR body still carries the first count (B5).

**Item 6 (ruling item 6).** The changeset's remedy list states: "A cloud migrate-and-exit job (`OS_MIGRATE_AND_EXIT=1`) must carry `OS_AUTH_SECRET` in production; without it the job is now refused, naming the variable." The no-secret text names it (`serve.ts:4709-4710`: set `OS_AUTH_SECRET` ... "A migrate-and-exit job (OS_MIGRATE_AND_EXIT=1) needs it too"), and the pin `:209-219` proves the job is refused with that text. `upgrading.mdx:421-422` and `cli.mdx:369-371` repeat it. The cloud seat's verification itself is outside this repo.

**Item 7 (ruling item 4, docs).** `cli.mdx:357` (the `--no-server` example) and `:365-371` (the flag description) are edited; `upgrading.mdx:413-426` is edited. No commit on the branch touches `content/docs/releases/**` (`git log` over the range is empty); `content/docs/releases/v18/index.mdx:61` still offers `--no-server`, as the ruling requires it to be corrected through the release-notes process. Every sentence the PR wrote is true against the code: the `--no-server` paragraph (refused before any plugin starts, migrate-and-exit included), the upgrade paragraph (no-auth refused the same way, earlier 18 releases let `--no-server` through and offered it as a remedy, `os dev`/`--dev`/embedded/host kernel unaffected, `os start` unaffected). One over-generalisation: `cli.mdx:357` "production still needs OS_AUTH_SECRET" does not hold for a stack that mounts its own AuthPlugin (cosmetic). Other places on the branch that still offer `--no-server` as the remedy for a missing secret: only the two the dev named, `.changeset/24583-7b3-organizationless-counter-retired.md:18` and `:24`, plus the release page the ruling reserves. `packages/cli/CHANGELOG.md:1131`, `:1733` and `serve.ts:632` narrate shipped history and offer no remedy (B6, B8).

### ② Semver level

`'@objectstack/cli': patch` with `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` on line-initial declarations in both the changeset and the PR body; a BREAKING banner; FROM and TO; a remedy list; and exactly one ADR-0087 marker, `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, a category the gate lists (`scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs:147`, `:287`). That is the level AGENTS.md:1087-1100 gives a non-protocol narrowing: `patch`, keeping its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition. `Check Changeset` is green on the head. Truth of the body: the TO, the Unchanged paragraph (including "`os start` always hands its `serve` child an auth secret, so it reaches the no-auth case only"), the `tenancy: { enabled: false }` sentence and the release-notes correction are all true against the code and the two files it cites. The FROM's "a production `os serve` / `os start` (no `--dev`) with `--no-server` booted the kernel" is imprecise for `os start`, which has no `--no-server` flag and always serves (B4). The remedy list matches the refusal texts: no-secret → set `OS_AUTH_SECRET` with the `openssl rand -hex 32` example (`serve.ts:4709-4710`); no-auth → enable auth (the `auth` tier or AuthPlugin in `plugins`) and set `OS_AUTH_SECRET` (`:4680-4681`); migrate-and-exit → `:4710`. Level and declarations correct.

### ③ Boundary flags

- B1 — not BLOCKING. `cli.mdx:399-401` still says a missing `OS_AUTH_SECRET` makes `AuthPlugin` "skipped with a yellow warning", which is false for every production boot except the host kernel and contradicts the paragraph the PR wrote at `:365-371`; and no `--preset minimal` mention (`:358`, `:375`, `:395`) says a production boot on it is refused. The sentence was already false on main for a `--server` boot since 18.0.0, and the `--preset minimal` consequence is item 1 as written, so it does not fail the ruling; the fix is one or two lines inside the claimed file surface and should be folded in before merge, with `--preset minimal` named in the changeset's FROM/TO.
- B2 — not BLOCKING. A production boot with the `auth` tier on and a secret set, whose `@objectstack/plugin-auth` fails to load, warns at `serve.ts:4573-4579` and boots with no AuthPlugin and no organization object. Outside the ruling's two named compositions and pre-existing on main; a card for the cli lane.
- B3 — not BLOCKING. A host kernel whose stack leaves the `auth` tier off is `auth-tier-off`, not `host-kernel` (`stack-auth.ts:181-184`), so in production it is now refused under `--no-server` too (it was already refused under `--server`). This is within the ruling, which keeps the warn-only path for the `host-kernel` reason, and the pins fixture the host kernel with the tier on; the cloud seat's item-6 check should also confirm its host compositions enable the `auth` tier. `ObjectOSEnvironmentPlugin` is not in this repo, so it is not measurable here.
- B4 — not BLOCKING. Changeset FROM names `os start` "with `--no-server`"; `os start` has no such flag (`start.ts:524-534`). Wording only; the Unchanged paragraph says the right thing.
- B5 — not BLOCKING. The PR body is stale: it cites head `5996c531`, omits the four `--preset minimal` re-fixtures and the green CI on `6531b332`. The dev listed the corrections in 6330837413; the seat should apply them before landing.
- B6 — not BLOCKING. `.changeset/24583-7b3-organizationless-counter-retired.md:18` and `:24` still offer `--no-server` (outside the claim's surface; the seat has asked for the fold-in). No other doc or code comment on the branch offers it as the remedy. `content/docs/releases/**` is untouched, as ruled.
- B7 — not BLOCKING. The pin file spawns ten boots (about 34 s locally) and declares no `test-budget:` line; the reader is `scripts/measure-test-shard-timings.mjs`, a report-only gate (AGENTS.md: a duration gate never reds a required job).
- B8 — not BLOCKING. The `serve.ts:632` header comment and `CHANGELOG.md:1733` describe a production `--no-server --preset minimal` boot as a past defect's command; historical, now unreachable in production. Cosmetic.
- CI on `6531b3324328c3310f23e01f66abe5933129758d`: 42 check runs, all completed, 36 success, 6 skipped (Console Pin Gate, the Dogfood Regression Gate matrix template, Dogfood Verify CLI, Temporal Conformance, Packed-tarball smoke, 18.x upgrade harness), 0 failure, 0 pending. Test Core 1/6 through 6/6, Build Core, TypeScript Type Check, Lint and Repo Gates, Governed Surface Queue Guard and Check Changeset are green.
- Size and governance: `check-governed-merges --branch` exit 0, NOT governed (0 of 10 paths hit the register), +346 / -81 over 10 files, under the 3000-line threshold.

**VERDICT: PASS**

Seat note: deliberate correction of a pending release note · epic PM `session_01Y5583bs2RDd53MH6kM1ca3` (`os-steve`) · 2026-10-22T02:24Z.

`Check Changeset` is red. That is by design: `check-empty-changeset`'s **DELIBERATE CORRECTION** class.
- **The note:** `.changeset/24583-7b3-organizationless-counter-retired.md`, 7b-3's pending release note from #24845. It has not shipped yet.
- **What changed under it:**
  - It said a production `--no-server` boot without an auth secret "still boots with the warning". It also offered `--no-server` as a remedy.
  - This PR executes ruling 6328987873 (#25133, letter A): a production boot that composes no organization object is refused whether or not `--server`. Both sentences are now false.
  - The PR rewrites them to the new behaviour: a kernel-only boot is refused the same way, and the remedy is `OS_AUTH_SECRET` or composing auth.
  - Restoring the note from the base would republish the false sentences.
- **Seat position:** the correction is right, and the seat widened this PR's file surface to that one note.
- **Who confirms:** a correction to a pending release note is a release decision, so the maintainer confirms it. The seat will not enqueue until that confirmation is on this PR.
